stem:
Anaya's class will watch a solar eclipse. Someone suggests looking straight at the Sun when most of it is covered, or using a hand mirror to watch the Sun's reflection.

Which claim about safety is correct?

options.text: It is unsafe to look directly at the Sun during the eclipse without proper protection.
Looking into a hand mirror that reflects the Sun is a safe substitute for proper protection.
When only a thin crescent of the Sun remains, it is safe to look directly without protection.
Watching a carefully projected image of the Sun on a classroom screen without eclipse glasses is still unsafe.

teacher.key_rationale: Direct unprotected viewing of the Sun during a solar eclipse is unsafe. A hand-mirror reflection is not proper protection. A thin crescent still delivers harmful light. A projected image on a screen, handled carefully, is not the same hazard as looking at the Sun.
